output.name: Halun

anatomy.part: base of the beak, where it meets the head
tip of the beak, holding the sand-eels
breast, at the root of the wing

output.myth: Halun was a puffin who fished the cold water under the cliffs for chicks that were always hungry. One winter Tavo the Gale came down the bay and shook the sea like a sail, and no bird could fly into it. Halun went anyway. He dived where the sand-eels hide and came up with his beak full, the silver eels laid crossways so he could not speak. He flew home against the wind with the catch held shut. His chicks ran to him and he gave them everything and said nothing. Aun asked him why he would not sing out his luck. Halun opened his beak a little, and the eels slid and shone. Hesk, who keeps count, wound a line for him and set him in the Windward Reach, where he hangs with his mouth full. Mothers say that when your father comes in with cold hands and nothing to say, you do not ask him. You take the fish.
output.verse:
Full beak, silent wing
he carries the sand-eels home
his mouth full, mouth shut
